summary: A modular monolith on AWS ECS on Fargate using Spring Boot with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL and a React Native (Expo) client. Chosen for a senior team of 8 with a $6000/month budget and 300,000 users in 12 months.

frontend.justification: React Native (Expo) targets android, ios, web, covering project.platforms=[web, android, ios]. It reuses the team's skills (team.languages=[java, kotlin, typescript]).

alternatives.why_not: Ranked 3.1 points lower: weaker on time to market (rated 4 vs 5, which your priorities weight at 3/5).
Ranked 5.8 points lower: weaker on time to market (rated 3 vs 5, which your priorities weight at 3/5).

tradeoffs: Native modules can force ejecting from the managed workflow
what_would_change: If the target platforms change (today [web, android, ios]), re-check coverage: Flutter is the next option.
If SEO stopped being critical and the app became highly interactive, a SPA framework would become competitive.

backend.justification: The team already knows java, kotlin (team.languages=[java, kotlin, typescript]), which Spring Boot uses. For a senior team of 8 engineers (team.experience=senior, team.size=8), Spring Boot offers a typed, structured API model (operations burden 3 vs capacity 5). requirements.ml_features=inference_api is easiest to integrate through a separate ML service. Its mature security and transaction tooling suits compliance=[dpdp, pci_dss, rbi_localisation, iso27001] (project.type=fintech). It can meet the requirements.p95_latency_ms=300 ms p95 target on AWS ECS on Fargate. It supports an MVP within timeline.mvp_weeks=16 weeks given its rating of 3/5 for time to market.

tradeoffs: Steeper learning curve and more boilerplate
what_would_change: If the team changed languages (today [java, kotlin, typescript]), re-rank: NestJS is the next best fit.
If scale.users_12_months passed 50,000,000, Spring Boot would need horizontal scaling and caching (cap = its comfortable range).

database.justification: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL suits scale.workload=balanced traffic with scale.data_volume_gb_12_months=500 GB after 12 months. For infrastructure.data_residency=india: it can run in AWS Mumbai (ap-south-1) or Hyderabad (ap-south-2) to satisfy data_residency=india. It is acceptable under compliance=[dpdp, pci_dss, rbi_localisation, iso27001] (attestations: pci_dss, hipaa, soc2, iso27001, gdpr). Its comfortable range (20,000,000 users) covers scale.users_12_months=300000. requirements.payments=true: transactional integrity favours a relational engine.

hosting.justification: AWS ECS on Fargate fits the monthly budget (budget.monthly_infra_usd=6000 USD): estimated $270-2400/month at scale.users_12_months=300000. It honours the hard constraint infrastructure.cloud_preference=aws. For infrastructure.data_residency=india: it can run in AWS Asia Pacific (Mumbai, ap-south-1) or Hyderabad (ap-south-2) to satisfy data_residency=india. It is compatible with compliance=[dpdp, pci_dss, rbi_localisation, iso27001] (the knowledge base records vendor attestations for pci_dss, hipaa, soc2, iso27001, gdpr); the legal obligations remain with you. A p95 target of requirements.p95_latency_ms=300 ms is realistic here. Availability target requirements.availability=99.95% is reachable with the platform's managed redundancy. scale.traffic_pattern=spiky load is absorbed by container scaling.

assumptions: Order-of-magnitude band built from each component's fixed + per-1k-user price estimate at scale.users_12_months=300,000; not a quote.
Traffic pattern spiky raises the upper bound by 25% for bursts.
The upper bound assumes components are not all at their high estimates at once (60% of the summed spread). Excludes taxes, engineers' time, payment-gateway transaction fees and SMS/OTP fees.

compliance_notes: DPDP Act (India): collect verifiable consent, honour access/erasure rights and notify breaches; the DPDP Act does not by itself require in-country storage, but the chosen India-capable regions keep options open.
PCI DSS: keep card data off your servers by using the gateway's hosted fields/redirect so your scope stays at SAQ A or A-EP; the hosting and gateway providers are PCI service providers.

RBI localisation: payment data must be stored only in India; hosting and data stores were restricted to India regions (it can run in AWS Asia Pacific (Mumbai, ap-south-1) or Hyderabad (ap-south-2) to satisfy data_residency=india).
ISO 27001 (iso27001): the cloud providers hold ISO 27001 certifications; certifying your own ISMS is a separate project.

Data residency india: primary data stores and hosting were limited to india-capable options (it can run in AWS Asia Pacific (Mumbai, ap-south-1) or Hyderabad (ap-south-2) to satisfy data_residency=india).
